title: Genetic Testing and Targeted Therapy in Solid Tumors
summary: Comprehensive genomic profiling (CGP) in advanced solid tumors increases identification of actionable alterations and facilitates matched targeted therapy, improving clinical trial matching and enabling tumor-agnostic strategies. Evidence supports first-line integration of CGP in many metastatic settings, utilization of basket and umbrella trial designs, and broader panels to expand therapeutic opportunities. Real-world data linkage refines prognostic gene discovery and outcomes benchmarking.
clinicalQuestion: How should genetic testing be integrated into the care pathway of patients with advanced solid tumors to optimize selection of targeted therapies and clinical trial options?

keyMoments.title: First-line CGP can guide therapy in advanced disease
keyMoments.body: A large cohort supports early CGP to identify clinically actionable variants, increase matched therapy use, and inform trial enrollment [1].

keyMoments.title: Adaptive trial designs accelerate access
keyMoments.body: Basket and umbrella trials efficiently test molecularly targeted agents across histologies or subtypes, with regulatory guidance supporting their use [3].

keyMoments.title: Broader panels expand opportunities
keyMoments.body: Broad panels identify more actionable alterations than limited assays, increasing chances for matched therapy or trial assignment [2].

keyMoments.title: Linking genomics to outcomes
keyMoments.body: Integration of genomic profiles with real‑world clinical data enables survival analyses to prioritize cancer genes and refine precision oncology strategies [4].

keyMoments.title: Recharacterizing diagnoses
keyMoments.body: Comprehensive profiling can reclassify tumor entities and refine precision treatment strategies, particularly in challenging tumors like CNS cancers [5], [6].

sections.title: Implementing Genetic Testing to Drive Targeted Therapy
sections.blurb: Operational steps to integrate comprehensive genomic profiling and translate findings into clinical action.

steps.title: Select the right test and timing
steps.body: Prioritize first‑line comprehensive genomic profiling (tumor and/or plasma) in metastatic/recurrent solid tumors where targeted options exist. Evidence supports early profiling to maximize matched therapy opportunities [1].

steps.title: Maximize sample quality
steps.body: Ensure adequate tumor cellularity and recent biopsy; consider reflex liquid biopsy for low-yield tissue or to detect resistance mechanisms. Re-biopsy upon progression to capture emergent drivers.

steps.title: Interpret and tier alterations
steps.body: Use standardized actionability tiers and consider tumor‑agnostic biomarkers (e.g., MSI‑H, TMB‑high, NTRK fusions) alongside histology‑specific drivers. Broader panels increase detection of clinically actionable variants [2].

steps.title: Match to therapy or trial
steps.body: Prioritize FDA‑approved targeted agents when on‑label; otherwise, pursue molecularly matched trials (basket/umbrella). FDA guidance supports these designs for efficient evaluation of biomarker‑defined cohorts [3].

steps.title: Leverage data integration
steps.body: Incorporate real‑world outcomes linked to genomics to refine prognostic expectations and therapy selection where randomized evidence is lacking [4].

steps.title: Reassess and adapt
steps.body: At progression, repeat profiling to identify resistance mutations or pathway bypass; consider trial enrollment targeting acquired mechanisms.

sections.title: High‑Value Targets and Clinical Signals in Solid Tumors
sections.blurb: Representative examples where genetic testing directly informs targeted therapy or trial selection.

cards.title: Tumor-agnostic markers
items: NTRK fusions → TRK inhibitors; durable responses across histologies
MSI‑H/dMMR → immune checkpoint inhibitors
TMB‑high → ICI consideration (context‑dependent)
RET, BRAF V600E in multiple histologies → matched inhibitors via basket trials [3]

cards.title: Common histology‑specific drivers
items: NSCLC: EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, METex14, RET, NTRK, KRAS G12C, HER2
Breast: ERBB2 amplification/mutations, PIK3CA, ESR1, BRCA1/2 (PARP)
CRC: RAS WT for anti‑EGFR, BRAF V600E (combo targeted), MSI‑H
Melanoma: BRAF V600, KIT subsets
GIST: KIT/PDGFRA
Cholangiocarcinoma: IDH1, FGFR2 fusions
Prostate: HRR genes (PARP), MSI‑H

cards.title: Brain and rare tumors
items: CGP can recharacterize diagnoses and identify actionable alterations in CNS tumors; supports biomarker‑stratified trials [6]
Reclassification via CGP can alter management trajectories [5]

cards.title: Pitfalls and limitations
items: Low tumor purity/old blocks reduce sensitivity; consider liquid biopsy
Variants of uncertain significance are common—avoid overinterpretation
Not all detected alterations are druggable; evidence strength varies
Access and turnaround times can delay decisions; plan early

cards.title: Trial design essentials
items: Basket trials: same drug across histologies sharing a biomarker; efficient for rare alterations [3]
Umbrella trials: multiple drugs within one histology stratified by biomarkers [3]
Master protocols can accelerate signal detection and regulatory pathways

cards.title: When to order CGP
items: At diagnosis of metastatic/recurrent disease with potential targeted options [1]
At progression to identify resistance mechanisms
When standard options are exhausted to enable trial matching, including NCI‑MATCH‑style approaches [7]

sections.title: What the Evidence Suggests
sections.blurb: Strength and directionality of current evidence across key domains.

cards.title: First-line CGP utility
items: Cohort data show increased identification of actionable drivers and treatment guidance when CGP is used up‑front in advanced solid tumors [1]
Real‑world genomic–outcome linkage strengthens prognostic and therapeutic inference [4]

cards.title: Broad vs limited panels
items: Broader panels yield more actionable findings and matched therapy opportunities than limited assays, especially for rare fusions or alterations [2]

cards.title: Trial enablement and design
items: Regulatory‑endorsed basket/umbrella designs efficiently evaluate targeted agents in biomarker‑defined populations, expediting access [3]
NCI‑MATCH framework demonstrates feasibility of genotype‑directed therapy assignment across solid tumors [7]

cards.title: Reclassification and CNS impact
items: CGP can recharacterize tumor diagnoses and guide precision strategies, notably in neuro‑oncology where histology alone is insufficient [5], [6]

sections.title: Operational Tips for Clinics
sections.blurb: Key steps to streamline precision oncology workflows.

steps.title: Build a testing algorithm
steps.body: Default to CGP for advanced disease; add liquid biopsy reflex. Define histology‑specific minimal markers if CGP unavailable.

steps.title: Create a molecular tumor board
steps.body: Standardize interpretation, tier evidence, and align on actionable thresholds; track outcomes to build a local learning system [4].

steps.title: Map trials and access
steps.body: Maintain real‑time lists of basket/umbrella trials and molecular eligibility; preauthorize common targeted agents and testing.

steps.title: Close the loop
steps.body: Document biomarker, actionability, therapy decision, response, and subsequent resistance findings to inform future care.
